re-trioceros-jacksonii.title: Jackson's Chameleon
re-trioceros-jacksonii.summary: A three-horned chameleon from cool, wet mountain forests in Kenya and Tanzania that gives birth to live young. It needs a tall, airy, planted enclosure, cooler temperatures than most chameleons, and daily misting; it's rated an advanced-level species.
rows: About 9–13 in total; males are larger. The yellow-crested form (T. j. xantholophus, the one most often kept in the US) can reach 14 in or more
Males up to about 9 years, females about 5–6 years
Tall, well-ventilated (mesh) enclosure: 18 × 18 × 36 in minimum for an adult; 24 × 24 × 48 in is better long term
Basking 80–85°F, cool side 65–75°F. Native forests run about 61–81°F by day and cool off at night
High at night (up to about 100%), falling to around 30% by day; let the enclosure dry out between mistings. Mist at least 2× a day
UVB is required: T5 HO UVB giving UVI 3.0–4.0 at the basking spot
Insectivore. Offer a variety of gut-loaded insects dusted with calcium; avoid wild-caught insects and fireflies
Handling is stressful. Let it settle for 1–2 weeks, then hand-tame slowly using food (offer insects from tongs or by hand)
Active by day; lives in trees and shrubs
South-central Kenya and northern Tanzania (Mt. Meru); introduced to Hawaii
notes: Gives birth to live young instead of laying eggs.
House one per enclosure; males especially can fight if kept together.
Most chameleons drink droplets from leaves rather than from a bowl, which is why misting matters.

re-furcifer-pardalis.title: Panther Chameleon
re-furcifer-pardalis.summary: One of the most colorful lizards in the world, from the coastal forests of northern and eastern Madagascar. Color depends on the locale it comes from (Ambanja, Ambilobe, Nosy Be and others). It's sensitive and needs a tall, airy, planted enclosure, UVB and bright light, and daily misting.
rows: 16–20 in (40–51 cm); males are much larger and more colorful than females
Males up to about 6 years; females up to about 3 years
Tall enclosure: 24 × 24 × 48 in (L × W × H) minimum for one; larger is strongly recommended
50–60% by day and 75–100% at night; let it dry out during the day
UVB required (about UVI 3.0 at basking height, e.g. a T5 HO 6% tube) plus a bright 6500K daylight lamp, 12 hours a day
Insectivore. Feed a wide variety of gut-loaded insects, lightly dusted with supplements
Active by day; lives in trees and rarely comes to the ground
Northern and eastern Madagascar (introduced to Réunion, Mauritius and Florida)
notes: Solitary: house only one chameleon per enclosure.
Locale names (Ambanja, Ambilobe, Nosy Be, Tamatave, Masoala) describe where the bloodline comes from and its typical colors; care is the same.

re-chamaeleo-calyptratus.title: Veiled Chameleon
re-chamaeleo-calyptratus.summary: A large, green-and-yellow chameleon from the mountains of Yemen and southern Saudi Arabia, easy to recognize by the tall casque on its head. It is one of the most common chameleons kept as pets and needs a tall, airy enclosure, UVB and a strong day/night humidity swing.
rows: Males 17–24 in (43–61 cm) snout to tail tip; females no more than about 14 in, but heavier-bodied
Up to about 6–8 years; females are shorter-lived (around 5)
Tall enclosure: 24 × 24 × 48 in (L × W × H) minimum for one; big males may need more
UVB required (about UVI 3.0 at basking height, e.g. a T5 HO 6% tube) plus a bright 6500K daylight lamp, 12 hours a day
Feed a wide variety of gut-loaded insects, lightly dusted with supplements
Active by day; lives in trees and rarely comes to the ground
Yemen and southern Saudi Arabia (subtropical to tropical areas near mountains)
notes: Solitary: house only one chameleon per enclosure.
Pied and translucent veileds are color morphs of this species.

re-furcifer-lateralis.title: Carpet Chameleon
re-furcifer-lateralis.summary: A small, colorful chameleon from the shrublands, forest edges and gardens of Madagascar. It's a short-lived display animal that needs a bright, well-ventilated planted screen enclosure, a cool night drop and water as droplets on leaves.
rows: One adult: at least 18 × 18 × 36 in (45 × 45 × 90 cm), densely planted with excellent ventilation. House singly and block the view of other chameleons
50–70% by day, higher at night, with surfaces drying between mistings. Water by misting or a dripper (droplets on leaves), not a bowl
Bright light with a linear T5 UVB tube and shaded areas; full darkness at night
Small to medium gut-loaded, dusted insects: crickets, roaches, flies, silkworms and locusts. Don't leave feeders in overnight
A display animal, not a handling pet
Madagascar (forest edge, shrubland, grassland and gardens)
notes: Keep adult females lean to reduce reproductive strain.

sources.name: Herpeton Academy – Carpet chameleon care guide

re-calumma-parsonii.title: Parson's Chameleon
re-calumma-parsonii.summary: Usually considered the heaviest chameleon in the world, a slow-growing, long-lived giant from the humid forests of eastern and northern Madagascar. It needs a very large enclosure, cool conditions with summer cooling, heavy water use and lots of large insects, so it's an expert-level commitment.
rows: Males commonly 22–27 in (55–68 cm) total length; females and C. p. cristifer usually about 20–24 in (50–60 cm)
One adult: 4 × 2 × 4 ft (120 × 60 × 120 cm) is a lower limit; a large male does better in about 6 × 3 × 6 ft (180 × 90 × 180 cm) or a planted room. Wide, anchored branches; house singly
Daytime air 21–25°C (70–77°F), broad basking branch 27–30°C (81–86°F), planted retreat 18–21°C, nights 15–20°C (59–68°F). Avoid sustained air above about 27–28°C
50–70% by day, rising to 80–100% at night with a real temperature drop and ventilation. Long morning and evening misting plus a dripper; good drainage
Bright full-spectrum light and a T5 HO UVB tube across a wide part of the canopy
Roughly 3–5 varied large insects every 2–3 days while active, gut-loaded and dusted
A display animal, not a handling pet
Humid forests of eastern and northern Madagascar
notes: Females need permanent access to a deep (12–16 in) moist laying area.
Color-form trade names (orange eye, yellow lip, yellow giant, green giant) are localities, not subspecies.
warn: Expert-level: plan air conditioning for summer heat before buying.

sources.name: Herpeton Academy – Parson's chameleon care guide
